finalText:
Same props ≠ same references. React compare by `Object.is`, not deep. Common causes:

**1. Parent re-render cascade.** Child re-render whenever parent re-render, no matter props — unless child wrapped in `React.memo`.

```jsx
const Child = React.memo(function Child({ items }) { ... })
```

**2. New reference each parent render.** Even with `memo`, these break it:

```jsx
<Child style={{ color: 'red' }}      // new object
       items={[1, 2, 3]}             // new array
       onClick={() => save(id)}      // new function
       config={{ ...defaults }} />   // new object
```

Fix — stabilize:

```jsx
const style = useMemo(() => ({ color: 'red' }), [])
const onClick = useCallback(() => save(id), [id])
```

Or hoist constants out of component entirely — best option when no dependency on props/state.

**3. Context.** Child consume context, provider value re-created each render = every consumer re-render, `memo` no help.

```jsx
const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, login }), [user, login])
<Ctx.Provider value={value}>
```

**4. `children` prop.** JSX children = new element objects each render, so `memo` on wrapper always miss.

**5. Custom `memo` comparator wrong** — second arg return `true` means *skip* re-render, easy to invert.

Diagnose: React DevTools Profiler, "Record why each component rendered" in settings. It name exact prop that changed.

Caveat: re-render not automatically bad. Re-render cheap unless subtree big or render does heavy work. Profile before wrapping everything in `memo` — `memo` + `useCallback` have own cost.

React 19 + React Compiler auto-memoize most of this. If on 19, enable compiler instead of hand-wrapping.
